newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Man fearing NATO invasion sets fire to Moscow flat.
newsitem.headline: Man fearing NATO invasion sets fire to Moscow flat.

text.p: A man set fire to his apartment and shot at firemen who tried to fight the blaze on Wednesday after convincing himself that NATO tanks were rolling into Moscow on the eve of a U.S.-Russian summit, police said.

The man, said to be mentally ill, barricaded himself into his flat in a northern Moscow suburb vowing not to give in to the "enemy" and, following Russia's age-old "scorched earth" policy in times of invasion, set fire to the building.
He shot at firemen with a starting pistol before police used a sniper to overpower him. He was then rushed to hospital with gunshot wounds, police said. One report said the man had died.
A fireman was also in hospital after being shot in the shoulder by the man, police said.
The incident took place a day before Russian leader Boris Yeltsin was due to meet U.S. President Bill Clinton in Helsinki for talks expected to be dominated by NATO's expansion plans.

Moscow fiercely opposes the Western alliance's plans to invite several former Warsaw Pact countries to join later this year, saying they threaten its own security and will create new divisions in post-Cold War Europe.
Many Russians remain deeply suspicious of NATO after decades of communist propaganda that exploited the country's traditional fear of invasion from the West.
Russians adopted "scorched earth" tactics, setting fire to villages and towns ahead of Napoleon's invading French army in 1812 and again in this century against German troops.
